newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Were puts "sell" on Hills.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Were puts "sell" on Hills.

text.p: J.B. Were Stockbroking has put a sell recommendation on Hills Motorway Ltd, the operator of Sydney's M2 motorway, and has estimated a fair value range of A$1.35 to A$1.66 a share, market sources said on Friday.
A Were report had estimated the M2 would generate long term average daily traffic volumes of about 49,800 vehicles, well below Hills' prospectus forecasts of 72,000 by the end of 1998.

Market sources said Were's fair value range had increased by about 10 cents since the initial recommendation three weeks ago because of falling bond yields, but it remained below Hills' closing price of A$2.05 on Thursday.

Hills announced on July 15 that average daily traffic in June, the motorway's first month of operation, was 39,801 vehicles. This prompted a sharp selloff in Hills' shares despite Hills' comments that it was too early to say what the long term volumes would be and that volumes usually increased in the first few months of operation as commuters learnt how to use it.

Hills chairman Stanley Howard told Reuters in mid July the company was considering a restructuring of its tolls on the motorway, possibly including a reduced toll for those using only part of the motorway. But Hills said then it had no plans to cut the A$2.50 toll for complete journeys.

Hills' shares have fallen from a high of A$2.42 on June 4 as doubts have emerged in the market about the validity of the 72,000 daily volume forecast. Hills is expected the average daily volume for July on August 14.
